corpus: Production as at 2026-09-24: 205 documents / 8,915 provisions, with corpus_stats refreshed 2026-09-24 04:14:44Z (provisions 8,915, avg_tokens 103.7493, drift 0). 107 WA acts, 93 WA regulations, and 5 Commonwealth acts - the Fair Work Act 2009 (Cth) in 4 volumes and the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) (352 provisions, compilation snapshot 2026-06-04). Measured after the 2026-09-23 Schedule-relabel and note-merge repairs, which is the state retrieval actually runs on. doc_type holds only 'act' and 'regulation': there is no award and no case law in the corpus.
note: Queries are paraphrases, not verbatim provision text, so the test is not trivially lexical. Targets are identified by citation and section, not by database id, so the set survives a reseed. The absent set must be re-checked whenever the corpus grows: two Fair Work queries were retired from it once the Act was ingested, because they stopped being absent. Section identifiers here are pinpoints, not row ids, so a labelling fix changes them: 'Casual employees of small business employers' was recorded as s 47A while Schedule 1's clauses carried plain numbers, and is 'Sch 1 cl 47A' now that they are labelled. Re-run this set after ANY splitter change, not only after a corpus change - a relabelled provision fails here silently and looks like a retrieval regression. Every known-absent entry carries the reason the corpus cannot answer it, and each reason is a checkable claim about what is NOT in the corpus, not an impression of difficulty. HISTORY on corpus_stats: this set was first scored on 2026-09-24 while corpus_stats.provisions read 8982 against an actual 8915 - a note-merge had deleted 67 provisions without refreshing the row, and BM25 reads N and avgdl from it. The row was then refreshed (8982 -> 8915 provisions, avg_tokens 103.0361 -> 103.7493) and the whole set re-scored. The effect was negligible and is recorded here so nobody re-opens it: max |delta| on a fused score was 0.00025, mean 0.00011, 74 of 81 queries fell slightly. Every headline figure was unchanged - highest known-absent 0.6669, recall ceiling 38/48, lowest zero-FP threshold 0.70 at recall 0.271. The only sweep cell that moved was FP at 0.60, 12 -> 11, because one known-absent query sat on the boundary at 0.600093 and landed at 0.599957. That is a tie-break, not an improvement. Per-query scores for both runs are in .orca/reports/2026-09-24-phase1-threshold-scores.json.  Case-law entries carry kind=case and, on the known-good side, the unit type the target is stored under; every case-law target is a numbered paragraph of a judgment, cited at [n]. They were added in the case-law phase and measured against the LOCAL corpus only.
